obtained.how: Wayback Machine capture (17 Feb 2017, openly downloadable) of the PDF the USGS National Wetlands Research Center served free; the old nwrc.usgs.gov link now redirects to a USGS center home page and the USGS Publications Warehouse record has no PDF. Noble (1965), the source of the growth figures, was read to check their length type: Wayback capture (16 Nov 2024) of the open-access UNI ScholarWorks PDF, whose live link sits behind a Cloudflare check (not attempted).

bibliography.checked_against: the title page and the report's own 'should be cited as' line (PDF pp. 3–4); USGS Publications Warehouse record fwsobs82_10_41
bibliography.note: Trial, J. G., Stanley, J. G., Batcheller, M., Gebhart, G., Maughan, O. E. & Nelson, P. C. 1983. Habitat suitability information: blacknose dace. U.S. Fish Wildl. Serv. FWS/OBS-82/10.41, September 1983, vi + 28 pp. As cited. The entry has no URL: the Wayback capture above (or USGS record https://pubs.usgs.gov/publication/fwsobs82_10_41) could be added.

claims.claim: 29 mm at age I, 45 mm at age II (under the table's 'total length unless stated')
claims.source_value: Trial et al. give 29 and 45 mm without saying which length; they are Noble's (1965) standard lengths — end-of-year means of young-of-year (28 and 29 mm SL in the two creeks) and age-I fish (44 and 46 mm SL). With Noble's TL = 1.23 SL they are about 36 and 55 mm TL. Noble's abstract itself gives 24–27 mm for age 0 and 49–50 mm for age I.
claims.quote: are 29 mm long by age I and 45 mm long by age II
claims.conditions: Elkhorn and Pease creeks, Boone County, Iowa, 1963–64; Noble measured standard length (snout to hypural plate) on 3,787 fish
claims.note: The lead from another reader holds. Mark the cell 'SL' (or convert to ≈ 36 and 55 mm TL) and say Iowa. Noble: 'Total length equals 1.23 standard length'; 'the age I fish averaged 44 and 46 mm' by the end of 1963.

claims.conditions: Trautman 1957 (Ohio), relayed; length type not stated

claims.claim: Maturity at age II; few reach III (Iowa; Noble 1965, via Trial et al. 1983b)
claims.quote: Noble (1965) reported that few fish reach age III
claims.conditions: 'usually mature at age II' (Schwartz 1958; Noble 1965; Bartnik 1970a; Bragg & Stasiak 1978); in Manitoba not until age III (Gibbons 1971)
claims.note: 'Iowa' is not in Trial et al.; it is Noble's study area (confirmed in Noble's title and abstract).

claims.claim: Fecundity 428–1,116 eggs (Traver 1929, via Trial et al. 1983b)
claims.quote: Females lay from 428 to 1,116 eggs, averaging 746 (Traver 1929)
claims.conditions: relayed from Traver 1929; fecundity rises with female length (Noble 1965)

claims.claim: Spawning from 21 °C in the north (Raney 1940), 15.6–22 °C, May–July, on riffle gravel < 25 cm deep at 20–45 cm/s
claims.quote: Water depths of less than 25 cm (Schwartz 1958), velocities of 20 to 45 cm/sec
claims.conditions: 'breed in May, June, and July'; 'temperatures ranging from 15.6 (Schwartz 1958) to 22° C (Traver 1929)'; northern spawning begins at 21 °C (Raney 1940; Scott & Crossman 1973); uniform gravel preferred; riffles the commonest sites
claims.note: Raney 1940 is relayed here; the references already mark it 'cited via Trial et al. 1983b', but the table cell does not.

claims.claim: Diet: chironomids and other aquatic larvae
claims.quote: eat primarily aquatic invertebrates, such as chironomids and other nymphs and larvae
claims.conditions: also terrestrial insects and plants; fry forage in quiet, silty shallows, larger fish in riffles and eddying pools

claims.note: Drift feeding is not mentioned anywhere in Trial et al. (searched the whole report); the nearest is foraging 'on invertebrates associated with riffles and deep eddying pools'. Source 'drift' elsewhere or drop it.

claims.claim: A stream fish of pools and gravel riffles in small streams, rarely found in lakes
claims.quote: typically are found in the pools of small streams
claims.conditions: 'rarely in lakes (Fish 1932; Scarola 1973)'; 'Adult blacknose dace typically occur in rocky and gravelly streams'; the lacustrine model has only a water-quality component because the species is rare in lakes
claims.note: The quoted phrase 'typically a stream fish' in §3.5.3 is Cooper 1941's, not Trial et al.'s.

claims.claim: Incubation at 15–22 °C; riffle sand to cobble at 20–45 cm/s; hatch ~5 mm
claims.quote: Water temperature ranges from 15 to 22° C during embryo incubation
claims.conditions: embryos at 7–60 cm/s, 'the majority are found at velocities between 20 and 45' cm/s (Bartnik 1970b); substrates sand (Raney 1940), gravel and cobble; nests in particles ≤ 2.5 cm
claims.note: The row's 'care: none' is not stated by Trial et al. (they describe a poorly made nest and, in R. a. meleagris, territorial males); the 5–8-d aquarium incubation is credited to Scharpf 2006, not checked here.

notes: Trial et al. give an upper incipient lethal temperature of 29.3 °C (Hart 1952), consistent with the 28.8–29.9 °C the paper takes from Terpin et al. 1976. The paper's 'Traver. 1929 … citation incomplete' entry can be completed from Trial et al.'s references: Traver, J. R. 1929. The habits of the blacknosed dace, Rhinichthys atronasus (Mitchell). J. Elisha Mitchell Sci. Soc. 45(1): 101–129. The follow-on fallfish mentions in the same tables cite Trial et al. 1983a (a different report) and were not checked here.
